world.title: Moscow car bomb injures former Ukrainian prime minister’s aide a day after fatal St. Petersburg blast
world.summary: A car bomb critically injured Sergei Zavorotnyi, 72, a former adviser to former Ukrainian Prime Minister Mykola Azarov, in Moscow on Friday, Nov. 13, Russia’s Investigative Committee said. The committee opened a criminal investigation but did not identify suspects. The explosion came a day after a car bomb killed a Rus
world.content: A car bomb critically injured Sergei Zavorotnyi, 72, a former adviser to former Ukrainian Prime Minister Mykola Azarov, in Moscow on Friday, Nov. 13, Russia’s Investigative Committee said. The committee opened a criminal investigation but did not identify suspects. The explosion came a day after a car bomb killed a Russian serviceman in St. Petersburg. Investigators did not identify the victim; local media reported he was a colonel or senior air force officer. A 2020 U.S. Senate intelligence committee report identified Zavorotnyi as an officer of Russia’s Foreign Intelligence Service involved in influence operations. Ukraine has not commented on either bombing. Azarov said he believed his former adviser was targeted because of his criticism of Ukrainian authorities.
world.image_alt: Moscow car bomb injures former Ukrainian prime minister’s aide a day after fatal St. Petersburg blast

world.title: COP31 negotiations stall over fossil fuels as UN chief demands cuts
world.summary: United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres called for an “immediate and drastic reduction” in greenhouse gas emissions on Nov. 13, as COP31 climate negotiations in Antalya ended their first week with countries divided over whether to set firm targets or specify a shift away from oil, gas and coal. The United Sta
world.content: United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres called for an “immediate and drastic reduction” in greenhouse gas emissions on Nov. 13, as COP31 climate negotiations in Antalya ended their first week with countries divided over whether to set firm targets or specify a shift away from oil, gas and coal. The United States did not send a government delegation for a second year under President Donald Trump. Turkey is promoting a global electrification goal, but its proposal does not require the additional electricity to come from renewable sources. The European Union supports electrification but says it should use clean energy. Australia is leading negotiations, with countries submitting views through Saturday, Nov. 14. A draft political text is expected early next week. Finance is also a major dispute: vulnerable countries say climate funding is arriving too slowly, while a recent assessment projects that annual climate finance could fall $840 billion short of a broader $1.3 trillion goal by 2035. The conference is scheduled to run through Nov. 20.
world.image_alt: COP31 negotiations stall over fossil fuels as UN chief demands cuts

world.title: Pope Leo celebrates homecoming Mass before vast crowds in Chiclayo
world.summary: Pope Leo XIV returned on Friday, Nov. 13, to Chiclayo, Peru, where he served as bishop, and celebrated an outdoor Mass at Pampas de Pimentel. The Vatican estimated that about 1 million people lined his motorcade route and roughly 500,000 attended the Mass, the centerpiece of his 12-day tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Pe
world.content: Pope Leo XIV returned on Friday, Nov. 13, to Chiclayo, Peru, where he served as bishop, and celebrated an outdoor Mass at Pampas de Pimentel. The Vatican estimated that about 1 million people lined his motorcade route and roughly 500,000 attended the Mass, the centerpiece of his 12-day tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru. The pope, born Robert Prevost, thanked the crowd for its support and prayers during his recovery from lung-cancer surgery about a month earlier. Prevost led the Chiclayo diocese from 2015 to 2023, after years of missionary work in Peru. Residents recalled his work with poor communities, Venezuelan migrants and people affected by floods and the COVID-19 pandemic. In his homily, Leo urged Catholics to combine evangelization with care for neighbors and practical help for people in need. Leo’s Peru visit continues through Monday, Nov. 16, with stops scheduled in Cusco, Pucallpa and Lima before his return flight to Rome. He is expected back in Rome on Tuesday, Nov. 17.
world.image_alt: Pope Leo celebrates homecoming Mass before vast crowds in Chiclayo

world.title: London police open serious sexual offences investigation into David Walliams
world.summary: London’s Metropolitan Police said on Friday, Nov. 13, that it had opened an investigation into allegations of non-recent serious sexual offences involving David Walliams, the British comedian and children’s author. Police said the new complaints were separate from allegations published by ITV News and The Guardian, but
world.content: London’s Metropolitan Police said on Friday, Nov. 13, that it had opened an investigation into allegations of non-recent serious sexual offences involving David Walliams, the British comedian and children’s author. Police said the new complaints were separate from allegations published by ITV News and The Guardian, but detectives are also reviewing those reports for evidence of offences. The reports accused Walliams of using his celebrity status to pursue young women and girls. One woman alleged he sexually assaulted her when she was 15, and others said he groomed them as teenagers. Walliams denies criminal wrongdoing and says he never abused his position. The Guardian and ITV said they spoke with more than 100 people during their three-year investigation. Police have not publicly detailed the number or circumstances of the new complaints. The force said specialist officers are supporting those who have come forward. Detective Superintendent Mike Cagney urged anyone affected to contact police, regardless of when an alleged offence took place.
world.image_alt: London police open serious sexual offences investigation into David Walliams

world.title: Turkey and Qatar sign pact pledging joint stance against attack
world.summary: Turkey and Qatar signed a mutual defense agreement in Istanbul on Friday, Nov. 13, pledging a unified position if either faces an external armed attack. The leaders agreed to consult on security threats and expand cooperation through military exercises, defense industry cooperation and personnel training. The public an
world.content: Turkey and Qatar signed a mutual defense agreement in Istanbul on Friday, Nov. 13, pledging a unified position if either faces an external armed attack. The leaders agreed to consult on security threats and expand cooperation through military exercises, defense industry cooperation and personnel training. The public announcement did not spell out how either country would respond to an attack. Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said the agreement would add a new dimension to ties with Qatar. He met Qatar’s Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani after the emir attended the United Nations COP31 climate summit in southern Turkey. The two governments said they also wanted to prevent renewed conflict in the Gulf and promote dialogue. They cited liquefied natural gas trade as an area for expanded energy cooperation. The pact was one of five documents signed at the 12th meeting of the countries’ Supreme Strategic Committee. The leaders also discussed Gaza, Syria and Libya, while the other agreements covered education, consumer protection and cooperation on peace and conflict resolution.
world.image_alt: Turkey and Qatar sign pact pledging joint stance against attack

world.title: EU names five-country team for Ukraine talks as Russia withholds approval
world.summary: European Union leaders agreed in Dublin that Britain, France, Germany, Italy and Poland, alongside EU institutions, will represent Europe in upcoming negotiations to end Russia’s war in Ukraine. The decision followed months of disagreement over whether Europe should send one representative or a team. It is intended to
world.content: European Union leaders agreed in Dublin that Britain, France, Germany, Italy and Poland, alongside EU institutions, will represent Europe in upcoming negotiations to end Russia’s war in Ukraine. The decision followed months of disagreement over whether Europe should send one representative or a team. It is intended to secure European participation in a process led by the United States, Russia and Ukraine. Officials from the five countries and the EU attended discussions on the sidelines of the U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi but were excluded from the main negotiating table. EU officials said the delegation is likely to include national security advisers and representatives of the European Commission and European Council; NATO is also expected to take part. Moscow has not confirmed whether it will accept the European team. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Russia would decide after assessing whether European governments genuinely sought to advance peace, while Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova said the issue had not been discussed with U.S. envoys. European leaders also rejected Russia’s push to discuss the continent’s security framework before addressing the war’s immediate issues. The next round of talks is expected later this month.
world.image_alt: EU names five-country team for Ukraine talks as Russia withholds approval

world.title: Suspected drones trigger U.S. security response at RAF Lakenheath
world.summary: U.S. Air Force security personnel responded to suspected unauthorized drone activity over RAF Lakenheath in Suffolk, eastern England, on Friday, Nov. 13. U.S. and British officials said no personnel, aircraft or infrastructure were affected and the incident was resolved. The U.K. Ministry of Defence said it was working
world.content: U.S. Air Force security personnel responded to suspected unauthorized drone activity over RAF Lakenheath in Suffolk, eastern England, on Friday, Nov. 13. U.S. and British officials said no personnel, aircraft or infrastructure were affected and the incident was resolved. The U.K. Ministry of Defence said it was working with U.S. forces to establish what happened. A warning instructed personnel to shelter in place, according to Sky News reporting cited by the Financial Times. Sirens were also reported at the base. The U.S. Air Force has not specified how many drones may have been involved or how security personnel responded. U.S.-used British bases tightened security after a September incident near RAF Fairford, where three men have been charged in the United States over an alleged plot. U.S. aircraft were also relocated from RAF Mildenhall. Iran has denied involvement in the Fairford case. Its security chief has threatened U.S. bases in Europe if they are used to attack Iran.
world.image_alt: Suspected drones trigger U.S. security response at RAF Lakenheath

world.title: US Treasury chief says Commerce delayed blacklist for Nvidia chip buyer
world.summary: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Friday accused the Commerce Department, led by Howard Lutnick, of failing for months to blacklist Singapore-based Megaspeed, an Nvidia customer suspected of routing advanced chips to China. Authorities are investigating the alleged chip diversion and the relationship between for
world.content: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Friday accused the Commerce Department, led by Howard Lutnick, of failing for months to blacklist Singapore-based Megaspeed, an Nvidia customer suspected of routing advanced chips to China. Authorities are investigating the alleged chip diversion and the relationship between former Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang and Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, whom U.S. intelligence suspects of working for China. Beijing denies the espionage allegation. Bessent said the Treasury, Defense and State departments, along with the U.S. Trade Representative, had supported adding Megaspeed to the Commerce Department’s Entity List, which restricts access to U.S. technology. He said existing export-control authority was sufficient and questioned whether Nvidia adequately vetted its customer. Megaspeed has denied wrongdoing and said it takes U.S. export rules seriously. Lutnick has agreed to testify voluntarily before the Senate Banking Committee, and lawmakers have requested testimony from other Commerce officials and Nvidia representatives. The Justice Department is investigating whether Megaspeed violated export laws.
world.image_alt: US Treasury chief says Commerce delayed blacklist for Nvidia chip buyer

business.title: Social Security retirement fund projected to cover 78% of benefits by 2032
business.summary: Social Security’s retirement and survivors trust fund is projected to exhaust its reserves in late 2032, leaving incoming revenue sufficient to pay about 78% of scheduled benefits unless Congress acts. Payments would continue, but retirement and survivor benefits would fall by an estimated 22% under the latest trustees
business.content: Social Security’s retirement and survivors trust fund is projected to exhaust its reserves in late 2032, leaving incoming revenue sufficient to pay about 78% of scheduled benefits unless Congress acts. Payments would continue, but retirement and survivor benefits would fall by an estimated 22% under the latest trustees’ projection. A separate analysis by the Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget modeled a 24% cut and estimated an average monthly loss of $500 nationwide, with reductions above $500 in 28 states and Washington, D.C.. In Michigan, the group estimated that about 2 million people could be affected and the average recipient could lose $523 a month; those figures use 2024 beneficiary data and a larger hypothetical cut than the trustees’ current estimate.
business.image_alt: Social Security retirement fund projected to cover 78% of benefits by 2032

business.title: Chicago Fed’s Goolsbee says Fed must restore inflation credibility as Bessent opposes hikes over energy shock
business.summary: Chicago Federal Reserve President Austan Goolsbee said the central bank has more work to do to restore its credibility as inflation remains above target, arguing that price pressures extend beyond oil and tariffs into services and medical care. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the Fed should not raise rates i
business.content: Chicago Federal Reserve President Austan Goolsbee said the central bank has more work to do to restore its credibility as inflation remains above target, arguing that price pressures extend beyond oil and tariffs into services and medical care. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the Fed should not raise rates in response to an energy supply shock tied to the Iran war. Goolsbee also cited strong demand from the artificial-intelligence data-center buildout as an inflation risk. Markets were pricing in a quarter-point rate increase at the Federal Open Market Committee’s Dec. 8-9 meeting, with a more than 10% chance of a half-point hike, CNBC reported.
business.image_alt: Chicago Fed’s Goolsbee says Fed must restore inflation credibility as Bessent opposes hikes over energy shock

business.title: U.S. officials keep Nvidia spy allegations off Trump-Xi agenda
business.summary: U.S. officials say President Donald Trump will not raise allegations involving Nvidia and a suspected Chinese intelligence operation when he meets Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen next week. Officials said the economic discussions would focus instead on implementing the U.S.-China trade agreement and that Washi
business.content: U.S. officials say President Donald Trump will not raise allegations involving Nvidia and a suspected Chinese intelligence operation when he meets Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen next week. Officials said the economic discussions would focus instead on implementing the U.S.-China trade agreement and that Washington does not negotiate export controls with Beijing. The allegations center on Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed, a cloud-computing company under scrutiny over whether it helped route restricted Nvidia chips to China. Nvidia founder Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive this week after reports of a relationship with her; U.S. officials have not said the allegations will be on the summit’s agenda. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said his department had supported placing Megaspeed on a U.S. national-security blacklist for months, but the Commerce Department had delayed the effort, the Financial Times reported.
business.image_alt: U.S. officials keep Nvidia spy allegations off Trump-Xi agenda

business.title: Fed survey names AI top financial-system risk as concern jumps to 87%
business.summary: The Federal Reserve’s latest financial-stability survey found that 87% of respondents viewed artificial intelligence as a significant risk to the U.S. financial system, up from 50% in the spring. Respondents pointed to elevated AI-company valuations, cybersecurity threats and increasingly complex financing tied to AI b
business.content: The Federal Reserve’s latest financial-stability survey found that 87% of respondents viewed artificial intelligence as a significant risk to the U.S. financial system, up from 50% in the spring. Respondents pointed to elevated AI-company valuations, cybersecurity threats and increasingly complex financing tied to AI businesses. The survey was part of the Fed’s twice-yearly review and included market participants, economists, analysts and institutional sources. The report covered conditions through Oct. 28. The Fed said the financial system remained fairly stable overall, but warned that hedge-fund borrowing had reached its highest level since 2013 and was concentrated among a relatively small group of funds.
business.image_alt: Fed survey names AI top financial-system risk as concern jumps to 87%

business.title: Anthropic investors weigh AI lead and forecasts before record IPO
business.summary: Investors evaluating Anthropic’s planned multibillion-dollar initial public offering are questioning whether the Claude maker can maintain its lead over Google and turn rapid sales growth into lasting returns, Reuters reported from the IPO roadshow. The listing, which would be among the largest ever, is drawing strong
business.content: Investors evaluating Anthropic’s planned multibillion-dollar initial public offering are questioning whether the Claude maker can maintain its lead over Google and turn rapid sales growth into lasting returns, Reuters reported from the IPO roadshow. The listing, which would be among the largest ever, is drawing strong interest, but investors’ revenue forecasts vary widely, and some say the company has not answered key questions in meetings. Bank estimates put Anthropic’s 2028 revenue at $270 billion to $280 billion, while one investor who declined to participate forecasts revenue about 30% below the sell-side estimate. Investors are also debating whether Claude can expand beyond coding into knowledge work and sustain premium prices if rivals offer comparable models. The roadshow is scheduled to run through Wednesday, Nov. 18, when Anthropic expects to price the offering. Trading is expected to begin on Nasdaq the following day under the ticker ANT. Chief Executive Dario Amodei told an audience at JPMorgan’s New York headquarters that the company was not focused on the precise date or market conditions for going public.
business.image_alt: Anthropic investors weigh AI lead and forecasts before record IPO

business.title: IEA forecasts oil surplus as Gulf exports recover, diesel stays tight
business.summary: The International Energy Agency (IEA) says global oil supply will exceed demand by 1.7 million barrels a day in the fourth quarter of 2026, reversing its earlier forecast of a deficit as Gulf exports recover faster than consumption. Supply averaged 105.4 million barrels a day in October after rising 2.3 million from Se
business.content: The International Energy Agency (IEA) says global oil supply will exceed demand by 1.7 million barrels a day in the fourth quarter of 2026, reversing its earlier forecast of a deficit as Gulf exports recover faster than consumption. Supply averaged 105.4 million barrels a day in October after rising 2.3 million from September; continuing attacks on tankers and energy infrastructure have not stopped the rebound. The agency expects oil demand to fall by 2.7 million barrels a day this year to 102.3 million, with high prices and disrupted refined-product exports weighing on consumption. It projects demand to rebound by 2 million barrels a day in 2027, while supply rises by 6.6 million to 108.1 million barrels a day. That forecast implies a surplus of about 3.8 million barrels a day next year. Diesel remains scarce because refinery capacity and product shipments are constrained, and European diesel prices remain far above prewar levels. IEA member countries plan to release another 71 million barrels from emergency stocks by the end of February 2027, including 15 million barrels of diesel. The agency warns that renewed shipping attacks could disrupt the supply recovery.
business.image_alt: IEA forecasts oil surplus as Gulf exports recover, diesel stays tight

business.title: SpaceX aborts Starship booster catch as spacecraft reaches orbit
business.summary: SpaceX launched Starship’s 15th test flight from its Starbase site in South Texas on Friday, Nov. 13, but called off an attempt to catch the Super Heavy booster after a technical problem. The booster diverted to the Gulf of Mexico and exploded near the water; the upper-stage spacecraft continued into orbit. The spacecr
business.content: SpaceX launched Starship’s 15th test flight from its Starbase site in South Texas on Friday, Nov. 13, but called off an attempt to catch the Super Heavy booster after a technical problem. The booster diverted to the Gulf of Mexico and exploded near the water; the upper-stage spacecraft continued into orbit. The spacecraft deployed 26 upgraded Starlink satellites and was scheduled to circle Earth about 14 times during a roughly 22-hour flight before attempting to return to Starbase on Saturday, Nov. 14. The booster recovery was the first part of a planned double catch; SpaceX had not previously attempted to catch the spacecraft after an orbital flight. SpaceX aims to lower launch costs and increase launch frequency by reusing Starship. The rocket is also intended to carry Starlink satellites in larger batches and serve as a lunar lander for NASA’s Artemis program, which targets a crewed Moon landing as early as 2028.
business.image_alt: SpaceX aborts Starship booster catch as spacecraft reaches orbit

business.title: Treasury chief Bessent faults Commerce over Nvidia-linked blacklist delay
business.summary: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent publicly blamed the Commerce Department on Friday for not adding Singapore-based data-center firm Megaspeed to the U.S. export-control entity list. He said Treasury, State, Defense and the U.S. Trade Representative had supported the move for months. The dispute is part of an inquir
business.content: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent publicly blamed the Commerce Department on Friday for not adding Singapore-based data-center firm Megaspeed to the U.S. export-control entity list. He said Treasury, State, Defense and the U.S. Trade Representative had supported the move for months. The dispute is part of an inquiry into whether Megaspeed helped route restricted Nvidia artificial-intelligence chips to China. The company is linked to former Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, whom U.S. authorities suspect of working for Chinese intelligence. China denies the spying allegation. Bessent said Commerce controls the listing decision and should enforce existing export-control powers. He also questioned whether Nvidia adequately checked its customers and prevented chip diversion, while the Justice Department investigates whether Megaspeed violated export laws. Commerce has not publicly responded to Bessent’s criticism. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has agreed to testify voluntarily before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 10 about the department’s role in the matter.
business.image_alt: Treasury chief Bessent faults Commerce over Nvidia-linked blacklist delay

science.title: IOM chief warns climate risks could displace over 200 million
science.summary: Amy Pope, director general of the International Organization for Migration (IOM), warned at the United Nations climate conference, COP31, in Antalya, Turkey, that more than 200 million people living in highly climate-vulnerable communities are at risk of displacement. IOM data show storms, drought, wildfires, extreme t
science.content: Amy Pope, director general of the International Organization for Migration (IOM), warned at the United Nations climate conference, COP31, in Antalya, Turkey, that more than 200 million people living in highly climate-vulnerable communities are at risk of displacement. IOM data show storms, drought, wildfires, extreme temperatures and floods forced nearly 30 million people from their homes in 2025. Pope said governments spend billions of dollars on border security while underfunding adaptation measures that could help communities remain in place. She estimated the cost of those measures at about $310 billion, compared with roughly $30 billion in funding so far. She argued that helping communities adapt before displacement occurs is more humane and cost-effective than responding to irregular migration after it begins.
science.image_alt: IOM chief warns climate risks could displace over 200 million

science.title: Geologists rule out proposed origins for Stonehenge’s six-ton Altar Stone
science.summary: A new geological study has ruled out several proposed source locations for Stonehenge’s six-ton Altar Stone but has not identified where the sandstone originated. Earlier research shifted the leading hypothesis from west Wales to northeast Scotland, though the stone’s precise origin remains unresolved. Researchers exam
science.content: A new geological study has ruled out several proposed source locations for Stonehenge’s six-ton Altar Stone but has not identified where the sandstone originated. Earlier research shifted the leading hypothesis from west Wales to northeast Scotland, though the stone’s precise origin remains unresolved. Researchers examined the mineral, chemical, structural and isotopic characteristics of the stone and museum-held fragments to identify features that any source site must match. The study was published in the Journal of the Geological Society on Nov. 5, and the report describes it as the most comprehensive geological investigation of the stone to date.
science.image_alt: Geologists rule out proposed origins for Stonehenge’s six-ton Altar Stone

science.title: Super El Niño warms Pacific, threatens California marine life and snowpack
science.summary: The U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration’s (NOAA) Climate Prediction Center said the developing El Niño is likely to remain strong to very strong through March 2027, with ocean temperatures still rising. The event is already associated with unusually warm waters off California, higher coastal water leve
science.content: The U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration’s (NOAA) Climate Prediction Center said the developing El Niño is likely to remain strong to very strong through March 2027, with ocean temperatures still rising. The event is already associated with unusually warm waters off California, higher coastal water levels and changes in marine food supplies. Scientists report seabirds washing ashore and kelp forests under stress. The pattern can shift rainfall and temperature, and forecasters expect warmer winters in the Northwest that could reduce snowpack by raising snow levels. Scientists also warn that warm Pacific waters can increase the risk of coastal flooding when high tides coincide with storms. NOAA’s outlook says the event is expected to weaken early next year, while reports indicate its effects could continue into spring.
science.image_alt: Super El Niño warms Pacific, threatens California marine life and snowpack

science.title: Euclid survey identifies 15,000 lens candidates and ancient quasars
science.summary: Data from the European Space Agency’s Euclid space telescope survey include about 15,000 strong gravitational-lens candidates and quasars whose light dates from when the universe was roughly 5% of its current age, about 13 billion years ago. The dataset is part of Euclid’s effort to map the universe in three dimensions
science.content: Data from the European Space Agency’s Euclid space telescope survey include about 15,000 strong gravitational-lens candidates and quasars whose light dates from when the universe was roughly 5% of its current age, about 13 billion years ago. The dataset is part of Euclid’s effort to map the universe in three dimensions and investigate dark matter and dark energy. The release contains spectra from more than 160 million sources, while astronomers are beginning to analyze galaxy clusters and the lens candidates. Tuoi Tre reported that the number of strong-lens candidates exceeds the total identified during the preceding half-century. Researchers expect the first findings on dark matter and dark energy in 2027; the mission aims to map more than one-third of the sky by 2031.
science.image_alt: Euclid survey identifies 15,000 lens candidates and ancient quasars

science.title: U.S. loses measles elimination status after yearlong virus spread
science.summary: The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), the World Health Organization’s regional agency for the Americas, revoked the United States’ measles-elimination status after finding that the same virus strain had circulated continuously for at least 12 months. The U.S. had held the designation since 2000. The status indic
science.content: The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), the World Health Organization’s regional agency for the Americas, revoked the United States’ measles-elimination status after finding that the same virus strain had circulated continuously for at least 12 months. The U.S. had held the designation since 2000. The status indicates that sustained domestic transmission has been interrupted, not that imported cases never occur. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reported 5,412 confirmed cases in 2026 as of Nov. 12, more than twice the 2,289 reported in 2025. State officials have reported 10 measles-associated deaths this year, while the CDC’s latest cited figures listed six. To regain the designation, the U.S. must stop transmission and remain free of an outbreak for at least 12 months. CDC Director Erica Schwartz said the agency would continue working with states on immunization.
science.image_alt: U.S. loses measles elimination status after yearlong virus spread

science.title: GLP-1 drugs studied for arthritis pain, addiction and aging
science.summary: The experimental GLP-1 drug retatrutide reduced knee pain in two phase 3 trials: about two-thirds of participants taking it reported at least a 50% reduction, compared with 38% who received a placebo. The trials involved adults with painful knee osteoarthritis, obesity and no diabetes. Separately, the GLP-1 drug semagl
science.content: The experimental GLP-1 drug retatrutide reduced knee pain in two phase 3 trials: about two-thirds of participants taking it reported at least a 50% reduction, compared with 38% who received a placebo. The trials involved adults with painful knee osteoarthritis, obesity and no diabetes. Separately, the GLP-1 drug semaglutide extended median life span by about 12% in older female mice, from 742 to 834 days; researchers also observed less inflammation and preserved cognitive and muscle function. Evidence for other proposed uses is less conclusive. A study of health records from more than 600,000 veterans with Type 2 diabetes linked GLP-1 use to lower rates of substance-use disorders, but the data cannot establish that the medicines caused the difference. Researchers say controlled human trials are needed to test these potential effects; the mouse longevity finding does not show that the drugs extend human life.
science.image_alt: GLP-1 drugs studied for arthritis pain, addiction and aging

science.title: Record-early polar vortex reversal raises late-November cold risk
science.summary: A sudden stratospheric warming has weakened and reversed winds in the Arctic polar vortex unusually early, roughly two and a half weeks before any comparable event in nearly 70 years of observations. The disruption can alter weather patterns below, but forecasters say its effects depend on whether the signal reaches th
science.content: A sudden stratospheric warming has weakened and reversed winds in the Arctic polar vortex unusually early, roughly two and a half weeks before any comparable event in nearly 70 years of observations. The disruption can alter weather patterns below, but forecasters say its effects depend on whether the signal reaches the troposphere, where surface weather forms. Forecasts point to an increased chance of cold outbreaks in parts of the United States and Europe from late November into December, but a widespread or severe freeze is not certain. A powerful El Niño, which generally favors milder conditions, complicates the outlook. Scientists say the unusual combination has few historical precedents, making the timing and severity of cold outbreaks difficult to predict.
science.image_alt: Record-early polar vortex reversal raises late-November cold risk

science.title: Older adults show weaker brain-clearing fluid waves during sleep
science.summary: MIT researchers found that older adults had significantly weaker waves of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), which helps clear waste from the brain during sleep, than younger adults. The researchers used brain imaging and electroencephalography to study volunteers ages 18 to 39 and 60 to 84, linking the reduced flow partly to
science.content: MIT researchers found that older adults had significantly weaker waves of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), which helps clear waste from the brain during sleep, than younger adults. The researchers used brain imaging and electroencephalography to study volunteers ages 18 to 39 and 60 to 84, linking the reduced flow partly to weaker deep-sleep brain waves and diminished vascular responses. Separately, a study described in a paper shared on Reddit found that LSD-related gene-expression patterns in rats and mice ran counter to some patterns associated with human brain aging. LSD also reduced certain amyloid-beta-related changes in mouse brain-cell cultures. These are preclinical findings, not evidence that LSD prevents dementia in people.
science.image_alt: Older adults show weaker brain-clearing fluid waves during sleep

sports.title: No. 4 UCLA beats Illinois 22-14 to reach 10-0
sports.summary: Fourth-ranked UCLA beat Illinois 22-14 in the rain at the Rose Bowl on Friday, improving to 10-0 overall and 7-0 in Big Ten play. The Bruins led 10-0 at halftime, but quarterback Ty Dieffenbach left with an apparent left-arm injury. He returned late in the third quarter and led a drive capped by the decisive touchdown
sports.content: Fourth-ranked UCLA beat Illinois 22-14 in the rain at the Rose Bowl on Friday, improving to 10-0 overall and 7-0 in Big Ten play. The Bruins led 10-0 at halftime, but quarterback Ty Dieffenbach left with an apparent left-arm injury. He returned late in the third quarter and led a drive capped by the decisive touchdown pass to Semaj Morgan. Illinois cut the lead to 19-14 and threatened again before UCLA cornerback Scooter Jackson intercepted Katin Houser with 2:50 remaining. UCLA added a field goal to seal the win. UCLA reached 10-0 for the third time in program history. Illinois fell to 6-4, ending a four-game winning streak. UCLA visits Michigan on Nov. 21, then hosts USC on Nov. 28, while Illinois visits Iowa on Nov. 21.
sports.image_alt: No. 4 UCLA beats Illinois 22-14 to reach 10-0

sports.title: McIlroy shares Dubai lead, closing in on eighth season title
sports.summary: Northern Irish golfer Rory McIlroy and Englishman Tyrrell Hatton share the lead after two rounds of the DP World Tour Championship in Dubai at five under par. McIlroy carded a two-under 70 on Friday, recovering from three back-nine bogeys with a closing birdie; Hatton shot 69. A win on Sunday would give McIlroy his eig
sports.content: Northern Irish golfer Rory McIlroy and Englishman Tyrrell Hatton share the lead after two rounds of the DP World Tour Championship in Dubai at five under par. McIlroy carded a two-under 70 on Friday, recovering from three back-nine bogeys with a closing birdie; Hatton shot 69. A win on Sunday would give McIlroy his eighth Race to Dubai title, matching Scottish golfer Colin Montgomerie’s record for the season-long crown. Spain’s Eugenio Chacarra, who led the season standings entering the event, is four strokes behind McIlroy at one under; Spain’s Jon Rahm is three behind and also remains in contention. Two rounds remain. McIlroy and Hatton are scheduled to play together in Saturday’s final group, teeing off at 8:40 a.m. UK time. The final round is Sunday.
sports.image_alt: McIlroy shares Dubai lead, closing in on eighth season title

sports.content: New Zealand beat India by 244 runs in the fourth one-day international at Mount Maunganui, bowling the tourists out for 89 as they chased a target of 334. Fast bowler Matt Henry took 6-27, including three wickets in the opening over, after opener Will Young’s 125 helped New Zealand reach 333. India lead the five-match series 2-1. New Zealand can level the series by winning the final match on Sunday, November 15, while India can secure it with a win or a tie. New Zealand will then host India for two Tests, beginning in Wellington on November 19 and in Christchurch on November 27.

sports.content: San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Deebo Samuel will return for Sunday’s game against the Dallas Cowboys, but left tackle Trent Williams and linebacker Dre Greenlaw are questionable after injuries in practice. Receiver Mike Evans is out with Achilles tendinitis. Coach Kyle Shanahan said Williams hurt his shoulder and Greenlaw his knee on Thursday; Vederian Lowe and rookie Jaden Dugger would replace them if they cannot play. San Francisco also expects veteran wide receiver Keenan Allen, acquired from the Indianapolis Colts, to make his 49ers debut. Dallas has cleared receiver George Pickens to return after a hamstring injury kept him out last week. The teams play Sunday at AT&T Stadium, and several players in the 49ers’ secondary are also listed as questionable.

sports.content: The Netherlands beat Greece 7-0 in Amsterdam on Friday, with midfielder Tijjani Reijnders scoring a first-half hat-trick and defender Jurriën Timber adding two goals. Crysencio Summerville opened the scoring in the sixth minute, and the Dutch led 5-0 at halftime. Donyell Malen scored the seventh goal. Germany beat Serbia 3-1 in Belgrade, with an own goal, Florian Wirtz’s strike and debutant Brajan Gruda’s solo effort securing the win. Serbia scored once and finished with nine players after two late red cards. The Netherlands leads Group A2 with 11 points, with Greece and Germany level on eight before Monday’s final matches. The Netherlands visits Germany in Berlin, while Greece hosts Serbia; the top two reach the quarter-finals. Germany must beat the Dutch to qualify outright, though a draw could be enough if Greece loses. The Netherlands needs a point to secure its place.

The National reported that six of those jailed took part in t
sports.content: An Abu Dhabi court sentenced eight people to six months in prison after a hotel brawl involving mixed martial arts fighters Usman Nurmagomedov and Merab Dvalishvili; two other defendants received fines but no prison terms, according to reports on the ruling. The National reported that six of those jailed took part in the fight and two filmed and published footage. The court also fined the eight Dh300,000 each and ordered their deportation after they serve their sentences. Dvalishvili and his friend Saba Lazishvili were each fined Dh50,000 and released. The confrontation happened Nov. 11 at the Yas Hilton, where Dvalishvili was giving an interview before a Real American Freestyle wrestling event. Video appeared to show Nurmagomedov approaching Dvalishvili from behind and slapping him before a wider fight broke out. Dvalishvili and Lazishvili were both injured. Real American Freestyle chief executive Chad Bronstein said Dvalishvili was back with the promotion, and the fighter said he was healthy and ready to compete. Dvalishvili was scheduled to face Marlon Moraes on Saturday, Nov. 14, while Lazishvili replaced Nurmagomedov’s brother Umar in a bout against Urijah Faber. UFC president Dana White said the promotion was not discussing a deal with Nurmagomedov.
sports.image_alt: Abu Dhabi jails eight after Usman Nurmagomedov hotel brawl

sports.title: France beat world champions South Africa 21-19 in Nations Championship
sports.summary: France beat reigning world champions South Africa 21-19 at the Stade de France in Saint-Denis on Friday, November 13, ending a five-match home losing streak against the Springboks. Captain Antoine Dupont, wearing No. 10 but operating mainly at scrum-half, helped France take a 21-7 halftime lead through tries by Aaron G
sports.content: France beat reigning world champions South Africa 21-19 at the Stade de France in Saint-Denis on Friday, November 13, ending a five-match home losing streak against the Springboks. Captain Antoine Dupont, wearing No. 10 but operating mainly at scrum-half, helped France take a 21-7 halftime lead through tries by Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang, Théo Attissogbe and Louis Bielle-Biarrey. South Africa fought back through second-half tries by Cobus Reinach and Malcolm Marx, but Manie Libbok missed a conversion after Marx’s try that would have tied the match. Despite three yellow cards and sustained scrum pressure, France held on after Bielle-Biarrey’s late tackle disrupted South Africa’s final attack and Dupont secured the loose ball. France moved six points clear at the top of the northern hemisphere group ahead of the Nations Championship final on November 29. France next hosts Argentina on November 21; South Africa plays Ireland in Dublin the same day, with New Zealand’s match against Wales also affecting the southern hemisphere standings.

After Sabalenka broke serve to lead at the start of the deciding set, Svitolina won six strai
sports.content: Ukraine’s Elina Svitolina defeated world No. 2 Aryna Sabalenka 6-3, 3-6, 6-1 in Indian Wells on Friday to claim the last available place in the Women’s Tennis Association (WTA) Finals semifinals and end Sabalenka’s tournament. After Sabalenka broke serve to lead at the start of the deciding set, Svitolina won six straight games to close out the match. The result completed the singles semifinal lineup: Svitolina will play Czech player Linda Noskova, while Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva meets American Jessica Pegula on Saturday, Nov. 14. Andreeva finished the group stage unbeaten, beating fellow Russian Diana Shnaider 6-2, 6-1 in 55 minutes on Friday. Svitolina, the 2018 champion, returns to the tournament’s last four for the first time since 2019. Sabalenka ends her season without a Grand Slam title for the first time since 2022, despite reaching the Australian Open and US Open finals this year.
